newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS - Spin-off seen boosting Great Eagle.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Spin-off seen boosting Great Eagle.

text.p: Great Eagle Holdings Ltd's decision to spin off its Tai Shan Properties Ltd unit should enhance the property giant's earnings as the money raised would help it concentrate on higher-yielding projects, analysts said.
Great Eagle said on Monday it planned to raise between HK$2.31 billion and HK$2.50 billion (US$296-321 million) by spinning off its commercial properties arm Tai Shan.
Following Hong Kong and international offerings, Great Eagle would hold 73.15 percent of Tai Shan.

"After the reorganisation and combined offering, Great Eagle will focus its resources primarily on the development of and investment in residential properties and hotels," Great Eagle said in a statement.
Andy Chau, research analyst at Mansion House Securities (Far East) Ltd said the move was good for Great Eagle.
"By spinning off its commercial properties, Great Eagle can now focus its resources on higher-yielding projects such as residential apartments and hotels," he said.
These projects offers greater returns and higher growth potential, Chau said.
Through the share sales, Great Eagle "could be able to raise funds from the market and that would substantially lower its borrowing costs," he said.

Desmond Cheung, associate director of Vickers Ballas, said: "Great Eagle needs finances for its projects. The proceeds from Tai Shan's IPO would pay off about some HK$800 million in loans it borrowed from Great Eagle."
"Great Eagle can use some of the cash raised to develop other attractive projects like hotels," Cheung said.

Chau said after Great Eagle last month announced net profit of HK$1.06 billion for the year ended September 30, 1996, up 28.7 percent on the year, Mansion House revised up its net profit forecasts for the company.

For 1996/97, Mansion House raised its estimate to HK$1.264 billion from HK$1.041 billion, while for 1997/98, it raised its forecast to HK$993 million from HK$920 million. The lower figure for 1997/98 was because the company was not expected to book any exceptional items for that year, Chau added.
While he said the spin off would further enhance Great Eagles' future earnings, Chau added that it would be premature to give a figure now.
An analyst at a European stockbrokerage said he believed Great Eagle had chosen the right time to spin off Tai Shan.

"I am not very optimistic on commercial property. I think there will be a lot of office supply and office prices are not going to increase very much, so I think maybe this is a good time for Great Eagle to spin off its office property at the upside of cycle," he said.
Some analysts said Great Eagle was likely to consider spinning off its hotels in the medium term to further concentrate on residential property development.

"The prospects for the hotel industry are quite good," Mansion House's Chau said. "By spinning off its hotel assets, Great Eagle can reduce its debt further. It would enable Great Eagle to concentrate further on its residential developments."
Analysts said the company may ultimately become a holding company, owning majority stakes in other units with commericial or hotel interests.
They expect Great Eagle to spin off Tai Shan shares at around a 25-30 percent discount to net asset value.
Great Eagle shares closed HK$1.40 or 4.46 percent higher at HK$32.80 on Monday.
